mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days when the rate is falling.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return distribution in periods of declining FEDFUNDS shows no statistically significant positive mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% signals labor market weakness that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5% (i.e., the signal fails to predict negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous weakness in GDP growth (GDPC1 < 11400) and housing market activity (HOUST < 1950) indicates a contractionary demand shock, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return distribution in triggered instances (GDPC1 < 11400 and HOUST < 1950) shows a positive mean return (t-test p < 0.05) or Rank IC is negative.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production (INDPRO > 110) reflects robust manufacturing output and corporate capacity utilization, supporting earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return distribution in periods of INDPRO > 110 shows no statistically significant positive mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising payroll employment trend (PAYEMS increasing over the prior month) signals expanding labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return distribution in periods of rising PAYEMS shows no statistically significant positive mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index exceeding 200 indicates elevated inflation that triggers central bank tightening expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 200 (i.e., the signal fails to predict negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 200) signal a monetary policy tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return distribution in triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 4.5 and CPIAUCSL > 200) shows a positive mean return (t-test p < 0.05) or Rank IC is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market strength (HOUST > 1900) indicates robust consumer demand for durable goods and construction, signaling an early-cycle economic expansion that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return distribution in periods of HOUST > 1900 shows no statistically significant positive mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
